nodes.text: Mind the filings. Every key your hands have ever held is written in my ledger — or rather, in *yours*. I only read it back to the iron. If a door you loved has crumbled, I can cut it again. For a price that respects the rock.

choices.text: How do you cut a door from memory?

nodes.text: Sit, then. Name the door and lay the coin on the bench — the file does the rest. A true cut *hums*.

The seed of a place never dies — the key only forgets how to say it. Your hands remember the saying. I file until the iron agrees with your remembering, and then the door is the door, _to the last stalagmite_.
Because a cheap memory would empty the deep places of their worth. Three keys' price for one remembered door — enough that you still go looking, not so much that a loved door is ever truly lost.
